20260827213657_AddCurrentDerivationAndCh.reason: Adds defaulted or nullable document derivation and locator columns, backfills only unambiguous current rows, and adds constraints respected by the previous indexer, which writes null pages and does not read the new columns.

20260828161744_AddPartyGuestMessages.reason: Adds two default-false Party settings and a new guest-message table; the previous application ignores the new table and continues to read and write existing rows through compatible defaults.

20260829173856_AddDocumentVisualRetrieva.reason: Creates only new visual-retrieval tables, indexes, constraints, and an optional pgvector accelerator; the previous application neither reads nor writes them.

20260830221014_AddPartyGuestHubChallenge.reason: Additive Party challenge tables, indexes, and settings with disabled/default-compatible values.

20260901134021_AddPrintFoundation.reason: Adds only new owner-scoped Print station, enrollment, device, and job tables; the previous application does not read or write them.

20260905074138_AddPartyPrintStudio.reason: Creates only the three new party-print tables — profiles, idempotency requests, and the per-job source rows; the previous application neither reads nor writes them, and no existing table is altered.

20260905080901_AddPartyPrintCapabilityTo.reason: Adds one nullable PrintTokenHash column to party_album_links and a unique index over it. The previous application leaves the column null, and PostgreSQL treats nulls as distinct in a unique index, so existing links keep working and rolling back to that application writes nothing the constraint could reject.

20260905191336_AddPartyPrintPerGuestBudg.reason: Adds four NOT NULL integer columns with defaultValue 0 — two per-guest ceilings on party_print_profiles and two per-guest print counters on party_participants. Existing rows take the default, which reads as "no per-guest limit" and "nothing printed yet"; the previous application neither reads nor writes any of them, so rolling back to it leaves the columns at values the new schema also accepts.

20260905231112_AddPartyGameRuntime.reason: Creates only the two new party game runtime tables with their indexes and check constraints; the previous application neither reads nor writes them, and no existing table, column or constraint changes.

20260906000059_AddPartyActivityRules.reason: Adds two nullable columns and one NOT NULL text column with defaultValue 'binary' to party_challenges, plus check constraints the default and the nulls both satisfy. Existing rows take values the previous application never reads or writes, so it keeps creating and editing activities exactly as before against the upgraded schema.

20260906001707_AddPartyGameVotes.reason: Creates only the new party_game_votes table with its unique and lookup indexes and a value check constraint; the previous application neither reads nor writes it, and no existing table, column or constraint changes.

20260906004257_AddPartyDisplayHeartbeat.reason: Adds one nullable timestamp column to party_album_links. Existing rows take null, which reads as 'no display has been seen'; the previous application neither reads nor writes it, so rolling back to it leaves the column at a value the new schema also accepts.

20260907104555_AddPartyGuestIdentityAndM.reason: Adds one nullable timestamp and one NOT NULL integer with defaultValue 0 to party_participants, and one NOT NULL integer with defaultValue 0 to party_album_links. Existing rows take values that read as 'not retired', 'no greetings sent' and 'no message limit', which is exactly the behaviour before the columns existed; the previous application neither reads nor writes any of them, so rolling back to it leaves values the new schema also accepts.

20260908090627_AddPendingBlobPurge.reason: Creates only the new pending_blob_purges table with its primary key and one lookup index; no existing table, column, constraint or index changes. The previous application neither reads nor writes it, and it is written only by BlobJanitor, which is disabled by default. Rolling back leaves at most a few rows the old application ignores and the new one drains on its next tick.

20260909090022_AddTvDisplayAssignment.reason: Adds two columns to tv_sessions: a NOT NULL string with defaultValue 'general' and a nullable uuid, plus an index, a restricting foreign key to party_album_links and a check constraint tying the two columns together. Every existing paired television takes 'general' with no link, which is exactly the behaviour it had before the columns existed; the previous application neither reads nor writes either column, so rolling back to it leaves values the new schema also accepts, and the check constraint holds for every row the old application could write.

20260909164555_AddPartyAggregateRoot.reason: Party becomes the aggregate root. It creates the parties and party_media_sources tables, then adds a NOT NULL PartyId to party_album_links with a restricting foreign key and backfills one party per historical party album. The previous application knows nothing about PartyId, so every link it minted after the upgrade would carry the zero GUID and be rejected by that foreign key: rolling back leaves an installation that cannot enable party mode at all. It also removes the Party/ShowOnTv coupling, which the previous application still assumes. This migration therefore requires a short maintenance window in which Party is unavailable, taken deliberately in preference to a dual-write transition spread through the services; the rest of NubArca is unaffected and no token, participant, upload, message, print, game or face-search row is read or rewritten.

20260909204649_AddPartyMainMediaSourceUn.reason: Replaces the plain party_media_sources album index with a unique index over (AlbumId, Role), making 'one album is one party's main media source' a database rule rather than an application check. No table, column or row changes. The previous application already created at most one main source per album through EnsureForAlbumAsync, so every existing row satisfies the constraint and rolling back to that application writes nothing the unique index could reject.

20260909224245_AddPartyGuestContent.reason: Creates only the new party_guest_contents table with its composite primary key and one restricting foreign key to parties. No existing table, column, constraint or index changes, and no data is written. The previous application neither reads nor writes it, so rolling back to that application leaves rows it simply ignores and writes nothing the new schema could reject.

20260910171228_AddPartyMediaReferences.reason: Adds one nullable uuid column (MediaFileItemId) to party_guest_contents, one lookup index on it and one on the existing party_challenges.MediaFileItemId, and two foreign keys to file_items with ON DELETE SET NULL. Nothing is backfilled and no existing value is rewritten. Before the party_challenges constraint is created the migration checks that every existing activity reference names a file_items row, and if one does not it raises an explicit exception inside its transaction, leaving the schema untouched; it never nulls or repairs such a reference itself. The previous application never reads or writes party_guest_contents.MediaFileItemId, so its inserts take null; it writes party_challenges.MediaFileItemId only after confirming that the owner's file exists, which the new constraint accepts; and when it permanently purges a file the database now nulls the reference instead of leaving it dangling, which that application already renders as an activity without a picture. Rolling back to it therefore leaves only values the new schema also accepts.
